one_sentence: Miranda-Agrippino and Ricco (2021, American Economic Journal: Macroeconomics 13(3):74-107) develop a new high-frequency instrument for US monetary policy shocks that purges an information/signaling component from Fed-funds-futures surprises, and trace its contractionary effects on demand, labor and credit markets, asset prices, and expectations.

issues.original: The Transmission of Monetary Policy Shocks / Miranda-Agrippino, Silvia and Ricco, Giovanni / 2021 / Vol 13 / No 3 / 74-107 / ISSN 1945-7707
issues.reason: Cross-checked against the AEA article landing page (doi.org/10.1257/mac.20180124) and RePEc/IDEAS (v13y2021i3p74-107): title, author names and order, year, volume, issue, page range and print ISSN all match the canonical published article. No field mixing detected — the volume/issue/pages belong to this exact title, not to a differently-titled Miranda-Agrippino/Ricco paper or an earlier working-paper draft.

This is a Web of Science bulk-export artifact: WoS renders journal titles in ALL CAPS with a hyphen substituted for the colon in multi-part AEJ titles. The actual published journal name uses a colon, not a hyphen, and normal title case.

No doi field present. Confirmed via the AEA article page and independently via RePEc/IDEAS that this DOI resolves to exactly this title/authors/volume/issue/pages. Added for a durable canonical anchor.
Web of Science internal accession number, not a BibTeX standard field and meaningless outside a WoS export; stray metadata left over from a bulk citation-manager download. Should be dropped.

issues.corrected: (removed, or fold into issn if the style requires electronic ISSN)
issues.reason: EISSN is a WoS/Clarivate export field, not standard BibTeX. The value itself is correct (electronic ISSN of AEJ:Macro), but conventional .bib hygiene keeps a single issn field (print) unless the bibliography style specifically needs the electronic one.
BibTeX/BibLaTeX convention requires a double hyphen for page ranges so it typesets as an en dash; a single hyphen renders as a plain hyphen.
ALL-CAPS three-letter month is another WoS export convention; ordinary BibTeX month fields use either the bare number or a lowercase three-letter macro (jul).
